propositions.text: Applicant is Sathiyarajah Amarasingam seeking judicial review under section 72 IRPA of May 26, 2021 decision refusing permanent residence on H&C grounds
The decision refusing permanent residence on H&C grounds is unreasonable

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant Amarasingam seeks judicial review of a May 26, 2021 decision refusing permanent residence on H&C grounds and argues it is unreasonable.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is allowed and the matter is remitted to a different immigration officer for reconsideration

paragraphs.summary: The court allows the judicial review application and remits the matter to a different immigration officer for reconsideration.

propositions.text: Applicant is a 52-year-old Sri Lankan citizen who entered Canada on January 7, 2011 and made a refugee claim as a Tamil Hindu minority member

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant is a 52-year-old Sri Lankan citizen who entered Canada in 2011 and claimed refugee status as a Tamil Hindu minority member.

propositions.text: Applicant was detained and persecuted during Sri Lankan civil war and faced harassment in government-controlled territory due to suspected LTTE association

paragraphs.summary: Applicant was detained and persecuted during Sri Lankan civil war and faced harassment due to suspected LTTE association.

propositions.text: Refused refugee claim on March 26, 2012, finding attacks were criminal and threats generalized risk
Denied leave for judicial review on August 15, 2012

paragraphs.summary: The refugee claim was refused in 2012 as attacks were criminal and threats generalized; leave for judicial review was denied.

propositions.text: Applicant applied for permanent residence on H&C grounds June 21, 2012, refused June 24, 2013
Removal order issued December 23, 2012; Applicant did not appear due to fear of return

paragraphs.summary: Applicant applied for permanent residence on H&C grounds in 2012, refused in 2013; removal order issued but Applicant did not appear due to fear.

propositions.text: Warrant issued December 27, 2012; Applicant remained and worked without authorization
Warrant executed August 20, 2020; Applicant released with conditions

paragraphs.summary: A warrant was issued in 2012; Applicant stayed and worked without authorization until warrant executed in 2020 and released with conditions.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted second permanent residence application on H&C grounds August 19, 2020 citing establishment, children's best interest, and adverse country conditions

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted second H&C permanent residence application in 2020 citing establishment, children's best interest, and adverse country conditions.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted Pre-Removal Risk Assessment application March 16, 2021

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted a Pre-Removal Risk Assessment application in March 2021.

propositions.text: H&C application denied May 26, 2021 after global assessment; PRRA also refused by same Officer
Officer not satisfied humanitarian and compassionate considerations justified exemption under subsection 25(1) IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The Officer denied the H&C application and PRRA on May 26, 2021, finding humanitarian considerations did not justify exemption under IRPA.

propositions.text: Applicant had some establishment in Canada but remained and worked without authorization for prolonged period
Applicant failed to appear for removal December 23, 2012 and went underground for over eight years

paragraphs.summary: Officer found Applicant had some establishment but remained unauthorized and failed removal appearance, going underground over eight years.

propositions.text: Applicant did not attempt to regularize status until recently, showing disregard for Canadian regulations
This failure negatively affected the H&C application

paragraphs.summary: Officer found Applicant's failure to regularize status showed disregard for regulations and negatively affected application.

propositions.text: Insufficient evidence Applicant would be discriminated or mistreated as Tamil returnee or long-term resident in Canada

paragraphs.summary: Officer found insufficient evidence Applicant would face discrimination or mistreatment as Tamil returnee or long-term resident.

propositions.text: Applicant did not provide sufficient corroborative evidence of past mistreatment by army or paramilitary
Applicant did not establish anyone in Sri Lanka had ongoing interest to harm him

paragraphs.summary: Officer found Applicant lacked corroborative evidence of past mistreatment and ongoing risk of harm in Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows detention likely only for those with significant political activity, which Applicant lacks
Applicant presented insufficient evidence that anyone perceives him as LTTE supporter or sympathizer

paragraphs.summary: Officer found Applicant lacked evidence of political activity or perception as LTTE supporter warranting detention risk.

propositions.text: Discrimination against Tamils exists but Applicant did not show hardship level justifying exemption from legislative requirements
Insufficient evidence that Applicant's family in Northern Sri Lanka denied access to social services

paragraphs.summary: Officer found discrimination exists but Applicant did not show hardship justifying exemption; family not denied social services.

propositions.text: Applicant is resilient and can adapt upon return with family financial support
Applicant's Canadian work skills are transferable in Sri Lanka

paragraphs.summary: Officer found Applicant resilient, able to adapt with family support, and has transferable skills for Sri Lanka.

propositions.text: Whether the Officer’s decision to refuse the H&C application was reasonable

paragraphs.summary: The issue is whether the Officer’s refusal of the H&C application was reasonable.

propositions.text: Standard of review is reasonableness as per Vavilov, requiring coherent, rational, justified decision

paragraphs.summary: The standard of review is reasonableness per Vavilov, requiring coherent, rational, justified decisions.

propositions.text: Court intervenes only if serious shortcomings make decision unjustified, unintelligible, or non-transparent
Shortcomings must be more than superficial or peripheral to merits

paragraphs.summary: Court intervenes only if serious, non-superficial shortcomings make decision unjustified, unintelligible, or non-transparent.

propositions.text: Decision ignores relevant evidence and applies illogical reasoning, making it neither justifiable nor intelligible (Vavilov at paras 104, 126)

Reasonableness may be jeopardized if decision maker misapprehended or failed to account for evidence; illogical reasons include circular reasoning, false dilemmas, unfounded generalizations, absurd premise (Vavilov at para 104)

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues decision ignores evidence and is illogical per Vavilov; Vavilov states reasonableness requires accounting for evidence and logical reasoning.

propositions.text: Decision maker cannot selectively choose evidence and ignore contradicting facts; must consider and weigh all evidence and explain why contrary evidence is insufficient (Ehigiator, Barril)
Intervention is appropriate if decision maker did not mention contradicting facts and court cannot assess if key issues were meaningfully considered (Ehigiator at para 52)
Overturning for failure to discuss critical contradicting evidence is not disguised correctness but shows decision maker may not have grappled with key issues (Hiller, Vavilov)

paragraphs.summary: Court explains decision makers must consider all evidence and explain ignoring contrary facts; failure to do so justifies intervention (Ehigiator, Barril, Hiller, Vavilov).

propositions.text: Officer turned positive H&C factors into negative ones, contrary to jurisprudence (Singh)
Officer noted discrimination but used Applicant's resilience to justify conclusion he could adapt after removal

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer unreasonably turned positive factors negative, citing Singh and resilience used against him.

propositions.text: Officer ignored relevant evidence contradicting decision that Applicant could not demonstrate risk if removed after over ten years

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits Officer ignored relevant contradictory evidence about risk after removal.

propositions.text: Same Officer decided PRRA and H&C applications on same record
Officer copied PRRA analysis into H&C decision but excluded more relevant PRRA sections for H&C
PRRA analysis cited Freedom House 2019 and US State Dept 2020 reports on military presence and harassment of Tamils
PRRA analysis concluded human rights abuses against Tamils may persist and discrimination continues

paragraphs.summary: Applicant notes same Officer decided PRRA and H&C; Officer excluded relevant PRRA evidence on Tamil discrimination in H&C decision.

propositions.text: Officer either did not appreciate PRRA and H&C test differences or improperly excluded positive information from H&C decision

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer failed to appreciate test differences or improperly excluded positive evidence in H&C decision.

propositions.text: Officer ignored PRRA evidence of discrimination and repeated PRRA risk analysis in H&C decision, applying wrong legal requirements
Officer failed to consider relevant factors through humanitarian and compassionate lens, dismissing discrimination and adverse conditions

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submits Officer wrongly applied PRRA standards in H&C decision, ignoring discrimination and adverse conditions relevant to H&C test.

propositions.text: Officer considered whether discrimination amounted to hardship justifying positive H&C, finding insufficient evidence of family difficulties and support

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits Officer found insufficient evidence of hardship or family support to justify positive H&C.

propositions.text: Officer's overall assessment reasonable based on evidence before them
Officer considered discrimination evidence against similarly situated individuals and found it did not amount to hardship
Officer reasonably assessed current situation of Applicant's family and found no hardship warranting H&C relief

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues Officer reasonably assessed evidence and found no hardship warranting H&C relief.

propositions.text: Officer reasonably considered Applicant's establishment factors independently and gave negative weight in context of immigration history

paragraphs.summary: Respondent submits Officer reasonably gave negative weight to establishment factors within immigration history context.

propositions.text: Subsection 25(1) IRPA grants Minister discretion to exempt foreign national from criteria if justified by humanitarian and compassionate considerations
Section 25(1) text quoted in full in English and French

paragraphs.summary: Court states s.25(1) IRPA gives Minister discretion to grant permanent residence for humanitarian and compassionate reasons, quoting provision.

propositions.text: Applicants bear onus to satisfy decision maker that H&C relief is justified (Lee, Owusu, Prasad, Patel)

paragraphs.summary: Court states applicants bear onus to prove H&C relief justified, citing authorities.

propositions.text: Test for H&C relief requires exceptional circumstances causing misfortunes greater than typical applicants (Huang, Kanthasamy, Chieu, Jesuthasan, Kanguatjivi)
Applicants must establish exceptional reasons to remain in Canada or obtain H&C relief abroad
All relevant facts and factors advanced by applicant must be considered and weighed (Kanthasamy)

paragraphs.summary: Court explains H&C relief test requires exceptional misfortunes and all relevant factors must be weighed.

propositions.text: Kanthasamy holds applicant need only show likely discrimination, which may be inferred from group membership
Discrimination can be isolated or systemic and cumulative discriminatory events must be considered (Liew and Galloway, Divakaran)
Officer erred by requiring direct evidence of personal targeting, undermining humanitarian purpose of s.25(1) (Andrews, BCGSEU, Quebec (AG) v A)
Evidence of discrimination against others sharing identity is relevant and reasonable inferences can be drawn (Aboubacar)

paragraphs.summary: Kanthasamy and other authorities hold discrimination likely can be inferred from group membership; direct personal evidence not always required.

propositions.text: Respondent cites Shackleford relying on Kanthasamy that H&C should only be granted in exceptional circumstances to avoid becoming alternative immigration scheme

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues H&C relief should be granted only in exceptional circumstances to avoid misuse, citing Shackleford and Kanthasamy.

propositions.text: Applicant's argument that Officer turned positive H&C establishment factors into negative ones should be sustained
Officer noted Applicant's resilience and transferable work skills but used these to conclude Applicant could re-establish in Sri Lanka

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer unreasonably turned positive establishment factors into negatives, using resilience and skills against Applicant.

propositions.text: Respondent submits Officer reasonably considered establishment factors independently and gave negative weight in context of immigration history
Court disagrees with Respondent's submission

paragraphs.summary: Respondent argues Officer reasonably gave negative weight to establishment factors; Court disagrees.

propositions.text: Officer not allowed to turn positive establishment factors into negative ones (Singh)
Singh criticized use of positive establishment factors to deny H&C relief
Sosi and Lauture found turning positive establishment factors against applicants unreasonable
Positive establishment factors cannot be used to attenuate future hardship (Zhou, Brambilla)
Officer erred by applauding assimilation in Canada but using it to deny hardship in home country (Lauture)

paragraphs.summary: Court cites Singh, Sosi, Lauture, Zhou, Brambilla to hold Officer erred by turning positive establishment factors into negatives.

propositions.text: Officer accepted Applicant's resilience and work skills but concluded Applicant could reintegrate in Sri Lanka, an unintelligible conclusion
Unintelligible conclusion supported by Teweldemedhn, Li, Lauture

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees Officer's conclusion that Applicant could reintegrate in Sri Lanka despite resilience and skills is unintelligible, citing authorities.

propositions.text: Officer decided PRRA and H&C applications simultaneously on same record
Officers deciding both applications risk confusing distinct analyses and must keep processes separate (Ramirez)

paragraphs.summary: Court notes Officer decided PRRA and H&C together, risking confusion of distinct analyses, citing Ramirez.

propositions.text: Officer considered some evidence in PRRA but ignored same relevant evidence in H&C decision
Ignored evidence contradicts Officer's finding in H&C decision

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer considered some evidence in PRRA but ignored contradictory evidence in the H&C decision.

propositions.text: Omission to consider relevant contradictory evidence is unreasonable (Vavilov at para 128)
Decision maker cannot choose evidence fitting rationale and ignore contradictory evidence
Decision maker must explain why contradicting evidence was given little or no weight (Ehigiator at para 74; Rajput at para 25)

paragraphs.summary: The court states it is unreasonable to omit contradictory evidence and decision makers must explain why contradicting evidence is dismissed.

propositions.text: Applicant provided evidence showing Tamils face growing discrimination in Sri Lanka and he is part of this group
Officer considered that evidence but failed to consider it fully in H&C analysis

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Applicant showed evidence of Tamil discrimination which the Officer considered but did not fully analyze in H&C decision.

propositions.text: Officer had complete record and considered discrimination evidence in PRRA analysis
Officer excluded that evidence from H&C analysis though it remained relevant
Officer failed to consider and analyze relevant evidence in H&C decision

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer considered discrimination evidence in PRRA but excluded it from H&C analysis, failing to consider relevant evidence.

propositions.text: Officer either failed to appreciate PRRA and H&C test differences or failed to weigh contradicting evidence
Reasons do not explain why important evidence was ignored in decision-making

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Officer failed to appreciate test differences or weigh contradicting evidence and gave no explanation for ignoring important evidence.

propositions.text: Discrimination, harassment, or threats may impact Applicant if removed and are important in H&C process

paragraphs.summary: The court states discrimination and threats, even if not meeting PRRA test, are important in H&C considerations.

propositions.text: Correct legal test for H&C is broader humanitarian and compassionate factors, not strict hardship (Kim, Yanchak, Kanthasamy)
Officer erred by applying incorrect legal test

paragraphs.summary: The court states the correct H&C test is broad humanitarian factors and finds the Officer erred by applying an incorrect test.

propositions.text: Officer did not rely on most up-to-date evidence relevant to H&C assessment
Sri Lanka situation is fluid; Officer should have relied on recent objective evidence like UNHCR Guidelines
Justice Brown in Krishnapillai emphasized need for timely, up-to-date PRRA country condition evidence
Justice Brown noted delay in decision and deterioration of conditions for Tamils
PRRA should be based on up-to-date country condition evidence
Sri Lanka situation is fluid with new leadership, emphasizing need for timely assessment
Applicant lacked benefit of timely, up-to-date PRRA assessment (Justice Favel in Navaratnam)
Failure to consider recent country condition evidence and reliance on outdated evidence is unreasonable (Rasalingam)

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with Applicant that Officer failed to rely on up-to-date evidence; prior cases emphasize need for timely country condition evidence.

propositions.text: Decision lacks intelligibility and is not reasonable
Judicial review application is granted and matter remitted for redetermination by different officer
No questions for certification arise

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the decision is unreasonable, grants judicial review, and remits the matter for redetermination by a different officer.
